room: Camelback kitchen (parts/room-6.mjs) now builds clean: the one refused write (furnace at 16,3,14) was already placed by the Chimneys part's hearth_nook, so room-6 leaves that cell '.' and the stove stays in the build. make.sh exits 0 and the room-6 line shows 10 placed with no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE.</summary>

left: Other parts still REFUSE writes into earlier parts (not touched, not mine): Chimneys 2, Dogtrot porch 2, I-house west 1, Pyramid NW 2, Boarding kitchen-hall 1, Smokehouse 17, Bungalow kitchen 1, Bungalow porch 1. waste.what: Finding which earlier part owns the refused cell (16,3,14) meant reading parts-report.json and grepping the other parts by hand to find hearth_nook(g, 16, 3, 14) in chimneys.mjs.
waste.cost: about 3 tool calls and one grep across ~37 part files
waste.tool: parts-report.json should record the owner of each refused cell (the part and helper that wrote it first), e.g. refusedAt entries as [x,y,z,wanted,had,ownerPart], so the fix is one lookup.

waste.what: Deciding that the stove cell should become '.' was a manual check that the furnace was identical (same block, same facing/lit) before dropping the write.
waste.cost: one read of the chimneys hearth_nook call and a comparison of states by eye
waste.tool: a runParts option or report field that says 'refused write matches existing block state' (or a diff of states) would separate harmless duplicates from real conflicts automatically.

waste.what: Each re-run of make.sh to confirm the fix printed the full build log (about 45 lines and 8 REFUSED lines from other parts), so the room-6 line had to be grepped out.
waste.cost: 2 full make.sh runs and a grep to find the one line
waste.tool: a per-part filter such as `node build.mjs --only 'room: Camelback kitchen'` or a make.sh --part flag that reports one part's status without rebuilding everything.
